summary: Focused backend verification of the Aug 2026 'approved on /storeapproval but stock never moved' bug + the 2 fixes (warehouse_id matching in submit_issue, _has_sap_log_error downgrade). New suite /app/backend/tests/test_gm_warehouse_id_fix.py = 14/15 passing. BOTH described fixes are CORRECT and verified, including one real LIVE Radish/SAP call (attempted=True, ok=False, error='SAP rejected the movement: Source logistics area is invalid for external id MOV-9BFFC7...' - exactly the expected fail-safe behavior). Live SAP inventory confirms the ID shape the fix matches on really exists ('P2/P2-RM', 'P1/P1-RM', ... in CLOG_AREA_UUID). HOWEVER a NEW CRITICAL blocker was found: the running server still executes every movement in DRY-RUN despite RADISH_GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN=false, because server.py imports store_approval_service (line ~59) BEFORE load_dotenv() (line ~66), so the module-level GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN constant is computed from an env that does not yet contain the var. Live API issue through /api/store-requests/{id}/issue returned goods_movement {ok:true, dry_run:true} - i.e. still no real SAP write. Also found: pre-fix pending store_requests docs (e.g. the user's P2-000019/P2-000020) carry locations WITHOUT warehouse_id, so they will still show 'not moved' even after the fix - they must be recreated. Frontend smoke on /storeapproval Movement History confirmed an attempted-and-rejected movement renders 'Failed' in red (#B42318) with From Warehouse 'P2/P2-RM · RI'.

critical.issue: server.py does `import store_approval_service` at line ~59 but `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR/'.env')` only at line ~66. GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN is evaluated at import time from os.environ, which does not yet contain RADISH_GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN, so it defaults to True. Proven live: POST /api/store-requests/{id}/issue returned goods_movement {ok:true, dry_run:true, external_id:'MOV-CCEB9A'} even though backend/.env has RADISH_GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN="false". Net effect: the LIVE flip the user asked for has NO effect and no real SAP movement is ever sent. Fix: read the flag lazily inside _trigger_goods_movement() (os.environ.get at call time) or move the import below load_dotenv() (same pattern already used for auth_service).

Intermittent hard timeouts -> 502 Bad gateway from the ingress. Measured: local http://localhost:8001/api/store-requests took 89.5s and 117.9s on two occasions (same query returns in 0.002s when idle); public journal returned 502 (60s ingress cutoff) on 4 of 7 attempts, and 200 in 12.0s once (only 7-8 docs in the collection). Root cause is not the query - it is the event loop / GIL being starved by the long-running SAP background refresh jobs (bom cache 4684 items, sap_valuation_client chunk retries with 30s connect timeouts visible in backend.err.log at the same timestamps). Real user impact: /storeapproval renders an EMPTY table (no error) whenever the journal call 502s.

minor.issue: store_requests docs created before this fix have locations[] without `warehouse_id`, so the new match returns None and no movement is ever attempted (verified: test_legacy_doc_without_warehouse_id_does_not_move). The user's own pending/resolved requests (P2-000019, P2-000020, P2-000004) show 'not moved' / From Warehouse '—' for this reason. Existing pending requests must be recreated (or the docs backfilled) before the fix is observable on them.

Comment claims the flag is 'env-driven (not a code constant) so this can be flipped without a redeploy' - it is still read once at import, so at minimum a backend restart is required (and today it is never read at all, see critical item).

Stale suite from the removed manual warehouse/target-bin picker era (sends warehouse/owner_party_id/target_logistics_area_id in the issue payload). It no longer matches the fixed RM->SFG rule and will fail if run - should be updated or deleted by the dev agent.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'Failed' badge in the SAP MOVEMENT column has no title/tooltip, so the real SAP reason (goods_movement.error) is not reachable from this tab (it is only shown in the request detail view). Add title={row.movement.error}.

When GET /api/store-requests/journal fails (502, reproduced repeatedly), the page silently shows the '0 movement(s)' / 'No stock movements recorded yet.' empty state with no error banner or retry hint - indistinguishable from genuinely having no data.

action_items: CRITICAL: make RADISH_GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN actually take effect - read it at call time inside _trigger_goods_movement() (or move `import store_approval_service` below load_dotenv() in server.py). Today every 'live' issue is still a dry run (ok:true, dry_run:true) and no SAP write happens.
HIGH: investigate the /api/store-requests* 60s+ stalls / 502s caused by SAP background refresh jobs blocking the event loop (89-118s on a 7-document Mongo find).
Recreate (or backfill warehouse_id into) the existing pending store_requests docs - pre-fix docs will never fire a movement.
Add title={movement.error} to the 'Failed' badge in the Movement History tab and an error state for a failed journal fetch.
critical_code_review_comments: Module-level env-derived constants (GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN) are import-order-fragile; prefer a function-level os.environ.get() for anything that gates a real ERP write.

The warehouse_id plumbing itself is correct and consistent across sap_inventory_client -> inventory_service -> production_confirmation_service -> store_approval_service; live SAP data confirms the '{site}/{site}-RM' ID shape exists (P1/P1-RM, P2/P2-RM, P2W/P2W-RM, P4/P4-RM, P7/P7-RM, P8/P8-RM, P9/P9-RM).

_has_sap_log_error() works on the real SAP payload shape (verified against a live response containing <MaximumLogItemSeverityCode>3 / <SeverityCode>3 + Note) and correctly downgrades ok:true -> ok:false with the SAP Note quoted in `error`.

submit_issue() silently skips the movement when no RM location matches; consider recording a reason (e.g. goods_movement={'attempted':False,'reason':'no RM stock on file'}) so the UI can distinguish 'no RM stock' from 'legacy doc without warehouse_id'.

success_rate.backend: 93% (14/15 - the 1 failure is the real dry-run env bug)
success_rate.frontend: smoke only: Movement History 'Failed' rendering verified; journal endpoint 502s blocked 2 of 3 UI attempts

seed_data_creation: Temporary store_requests docs (requester TEST_QA_WHID / TEST_QA_UI, _id TEST_UI_FAILED_MOVE) - all deleted; store_requests count back to 7. NOTE: the P2 request/issue counters were incremented by these seeds, so the next real P2 request ID will skip a few numbers (harmless).
test_credentials: not required (/storeapproval is unauthenticated); Radish creds read from backend/.env
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/test_gm_warehouse_id_fix.py (run with -n 0; it makes 1 real LIVE Radish call of 0.01 KGM via TestLiveMovementWithFlagForced which monkeypatches GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN=False). After the dev fixes the import-order/dry-run bug, TestDryRunFlagPlumbing::test_env_false_is_honoured_by_running_server should pass and the live movement will come back ok:False with 'Source logistics area is invalid' - that is EXPECTED (open item: correct SAP Logistics Area ID string unconfirmed), not a regression. Beware /api/store-requests* intermittent 60s+ stalls -> 502; retry.
rca_of_the_issue: Original reported bug (goods_movement None / 'not moved'): submit_issue matched the fixed 'P2/P2-RM' ID against loc['warehouse'] which holds the SAP description - fixed correctly by the new warehouse_id field (verified end-to-end with a two-location component: the RM location, owner RI, was selected and source_logistics_area_id='P2/P2-RM' / target='P2/P2-SFG' were sent). Second layer of the same user complaint remains open: even with the match fixed, no REAL SAP movement can currently be sent because store_approval_service is imported before load_dotenv() in server.py, so RADISH_GOODS_MOVEMENT_DRY_RUN=false is never seen and every call runs as a dry run returning ok:true - the UI honestly labels it 'Dry Run OK', but nothing moves in SAP.
